process.d: Data model, API contracts and a permissions model — reviewed and approved before we build. Fixing an architectural mistake here costs an hour; three months in it costs a rebuild.

faq.q: How long does an enterprise system take?
faq.a: It depends on scope. A full accounting system with its modules is built in increments over months, but a first usable version usually reaches you within a few weeks of the architecture being approved. We commit to a stated schedule in the scope document, and tell you immediately if anything changes.

faq.q: Do I own the code after handover?
faq.a: Yes, entirely. We hand over the repository, the documentation, the deployment accounts and the database. We keep no key that forces you to stay with us.

faq.q: Do you work with clients outside Palestine?
faq.a: Yes. We serve clients in more than ten countries; the work is fully remote with regular meetings and a shared tracking board.

faq.q: Does Smart Accountant replace the accountant?
faq.a: No. It replaces the repetitive manual work: entering invoices, posting routine entries, reconciling balances. The accounting judgement and the review stay human — and the system is designed to make that review easier, not to bypass it.

faq.q: How do you handle support after launch?
faq.a: Every delivery comes with an agreed care period for defects, and an optional maintenance contract afterwards. We never make your system's survival depend on that contract.

faq.q: Do you take over stalled projects from another team?
faq.a: Yes. We start with a blunt technical audit: what works, what must be rebuilt, and the cost of each path. Sometimes our recommendation is not to rebuild — and we say so.

founderQuote: I started in 2018 from Gaza with a mobile phone and a slow connection. The goal was never just to have work; it was to prove that an Arab engineer can build systems measured by the global standard — not by a lenient local one. That is still the measure we hold everything we ship against.
